name: Image-Based and Splat Compression

# Image-Based and Splat Compression


## Overview
Image-Based and Splat Compression methods address the excessive storage requirements of [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) primitives by mapping multi-dimensional parameter tensors into compact 2D grid layouts [S1, unofficial] or structured binary streams [Splat parameter encoding and codec selection](5019-splat-parameter-encoding-and-codec-selection.md). These methods exploit the structured, heterogeneous nature of splat attributes using targeted [quantization](#5935-quantization.md) and codec policies to achieve significant size reductions while maintaining rendering fidelity [G].

## Shared principles
All [compression](#4-compression.md) methods in this family share the mechanisms detailed in [Compression](4-compression.md).

## Subtopics

### [Splat parameter encoding and codec selection](5019-splat-parameter-encoding-and-codec-selection.md)
This method defines the binary layout and compression pipeline for 3D Gaussian Splat parameters to minimize storage size while maintaining rendering fidelity. It solves the problem of excessive file sizes in raw Gaussian Splat formats (typically 30–37 bytes/splat) by applying targeted quantization and a width-aware codec policy. It differs from generic image compression [PngCompression](11785-pngcompression.md) by operating on structured, heterogeneous vector fields (position, scale, [rotation](#19376-rotation.md), amplitude) rather than uniform pixel grids, and by using spatial bucketing and [delta encoding](#1096-delta-encoding.md) specific to splat distributions. See [Splat parameter encoding and codec selection](5019-splat-parameter-encoding-and-codec-selection.md) for implementation details.

### [PngCompression](11785-pngcompression.md)
[PngCompression](#11785-pngcompression.md) is a lossy compression method for 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) data that encodes splat parameters into standard PNG image files. It solves the problem of storing and transmitting large sets of Gaussian primitives by mapping multi-dimensional parameter tensors into 2D grid layouts, utilizing 8-bit or 16-bit quantization for spatial/attribute data and K-means clustering for spherical harmonic coefficients. It is distinguished from other [image-based compression](#18716-texture-map-coding-tmc.md) methods by its specific handling of non-square Gaussian counts via opacity-based [cropping](#1648-cropping.md) and its hybrid approach of using PNG for most parameters while reserving NPZ for clustered [SH coefficients](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md). See [PngCompression](11785-pngcompression.md) for implementation details.

### Self-Organizing Gaussians (SOG)
[Self-Organizing Gaussians (SOG)](#6140-self-organizing-gaussians-sog.md) projects all Gaussian attributes into 2D maps, enabling the use of standard image codecs such as PNG, JPEG, or EXR for compression [S1, unofficial]. This approach leverages the spatial coherence of the projected attributes to achieve high compression ratios [G].

### Texture Image Storage
Texture Image Storage allocates 8-dimensional features across two 4-channel PNG images, totaling 8 channels [S2]. The alpha channel is squeezed into the first feature channel, where alpha equals one when the first feature channel is non-zero and zero otherwise [S2]. Large texture images are split into multiple 4096×4096 images to satisfy mobile hardware constraints requiring power-of-two dimensions capped at 4096×4096 [S2].

## Background
The need for efficient compression in 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) arises from the large memory footprint of raw Gaussian primitives [G]. Early variants like [LightGaussian](#8036-lightgaussian.md) (NeurIPS'23) introduced pruning and spherical harmonic distillation, achieving 15× size reduction with minimal quality loss [S1, unofficial]. Subsequent methods such as Compact3D, C3DGS, and [EAGLES](#7990-eagles.md) focused on [vector quantization](#907-vector-quantization.md) of spherical harmonic and scale parameters [S1, unofficial]. The Self-Organizing Gaussians (SOG) approach further simplified the pipeline by projecting attributes to 2D for standard image codec compatibility [S1, unofficial]. More recent techniques like Reduced-MS and RDO-Gaussian employ rate-distortion optimization at compression time, while [Hierarchical 3DGS](#5996-octree-based-3d-gaussian-splatting.md) introduces [octree-like structures](#2792-octree-based-structures.md) for level-of-detail rendering [S1, unofficial].

## Sources

[S2] MobileNeRF: Exploiting the Polygon Rasterization Pipeline for Efficient Neural Field Rendering on Mobile Architectures, https://doi.org/10.1109/cvpr52729.2023.01590, fetched 2026-10-26
